cards.text: Jesus has just finished teaching His disciples all these things. Now He has something to tell them about what's coming. Hold onto your apron, friend.

cards.question: Jesus tells His disciples a feast is just two days away. Which one?
True or false: Jesus tells His disciples the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.

cards.text: At that time, the chief priests and the elders of the people gather in the courtyard of Caiaphas, the high priest. That many big names in one courtyard, and I promise you, NOBODY is planning a bake sale.

cards.question: The chief priests and elders are huddled in Caiaphas's courtyard. What are they plotting to do with Jesus?

answers.text: Arrest Him covertly and kill Him
Debate Him in front of the crowds

cards.question: The plotters in Caiaphas's courtyard have one condition: not during the feast. Why not?

answers.text: There may be a riot among the people
The courts will be closed for the feast
Caiaphas will be busy at the temple

cards.text: Meanwhile, Jesus is in a town called Bethany, at the home of a man known as Simon the Leper. Different house, different crowd.
While Jesus reclines at the table, a woman comes to Him with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume. Not the cheap stuff, friend. The EXPENSIVE stuff.

cards.question: The woman pours her expensive perfume on Jesus' ___ as He reclines at the table.
The disciples watch the woman pour that expensive perfume on Jesus. How do they react?

cards.text: They ask, "Why this waste?" Friend, I once watched Mother Miller knock a whole bag of chocolate chips onto the kitchen floor, and I stared at that spot for a WEEK.

cards.question: True or false: The disciples say the woman's perfume could have been sold and the money given to the temple.

cards.text: Back in Bethany, Jesus is aware of what His disciples are saying about that perfume. He asks them, "Why are you bothering this woman?"

cards.question: Jesus tells His disciples the woman with the perfume has done a ___ deed to Him.
True or false: Jesus tells His disciples the poor won't always be with them, but He will be.
Jesus says that by pouring this perfume on Him, the woman has done something for Him. What?

answers.text: Anointed Him as king of Israel
Refreshed Him for the road ahead

cards.question: Then Jesus makes a promise about the woman with the perfume. What is it?

answers.text: Her deed will be told wherever the gospel is preached
Her jar will be paid back to her many times over
Her name will be written on the walls of the temple

cards.text: Think about that, friend. She walked in with one jar, and her story goes wherever the gospel goes, while I walked out of a closing sale with a 25-cent sticker stuck to my head.
Then one of the Twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, goes to the chief priests. Yeah. The chief priests who were just plotting in that courtyard.

cards.question: True or false: Judas Iscariot asks the chief priests what they're willing to give him if he hands Jesus over.
The chief priests set out ___ pieces of silver for Judas Iscariot.

cards.text: From then on, Judas looks for an opportunity to betray Jesus. That's where we pause, friend, and believe me, this story is just getting started.

findings.problem: "Jesus has just finished teaching His disciples all these things" names the disciples as the audience for "all these things." Matthew 26:1 only says Jesus finished saying all these things and then spoke to His disciples. The teaching before this included crowds (Matt 23:1). The card also doesn't say what "all these things" were, even though the passage opens in the middle of a thought.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The opening card doesn't give the context for "all these things," which points back to teaching that comes before this passage.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: "Meanwhile" says the anointing happens at the same time as the plot in Caiaphas's courtyard. Matthew 26:6 says only "While Jesus was in Bethany" and gives no timing relative to 26:3-5.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: "While Jesus reclines... perfume." / "Not the cheap stuff, friend." / "The EXPENSIVE stuff."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new event in the Millers' kitchen: Mother Miller spilling a bag of chocolate chips, and Papa Dorin staring at the spot for a week. Jokes may make up small moments around his bakery, but they can't add to his backstory.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The right answer "beautiful" is the only positive word. "Foolish" and "careless" are both negative. Card 1 has just shown Jesus defending the woman, so the right answer stands out and the wrong answers are ruled out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card adds no new part of the passage. It repeats the answer to card 5 (her story goes wherever the gospel goes) and only adds a joke.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't match the core action. Her deed is being remembered wherever the gospel goes. His half of the joke is about being sold cheap. A baker could easily say "huh?" The card also invents a backstory detail: the 25-cent sticker "stuck to my head."

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: "Then one of the Twelve... goes to the chief priests." / "Yeah." / "The chief priests who were just plotting in that courtyard." The word "just" also adds timing the text doesn't give.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
